title: Dry Scrubber
model_title: Dry Scrubber — Dry Sorbent Injection (Hydrated Lime / Sodium Bicarbonate) with Reaction Chamber & Recirculation

introduction.definition: A dry scrubber removes acid gases by injecting fine dry sorbent — hydrated lime or sodium bicarbonate — into the flue gas. The sorbent reacts with SO₂ and HCl in a reaction chamber; the dry product and unreacted sorbent are captured in a fabric filter, partly recirculated, and disposed of as powder with no wastewater.
applications: Waste incinerators, biomass and small coal boilers
introduction.summary: A dry scrubber removes acid gases by injecting a fine dry sorbent (hydrated lime or sodium bicarbonate) into the flue gas; the reacted powder is collected downstream in a fabric filter, with no liquid effluent.

pressure.title: Acid gas falls as sorbent reacts
pressure.description: Fine dry sorbent injected into the hot flue gas reacts with acid gases: Ca(OH)₂ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + H₂O, Ca(OH)₂ + 2 HCl → CaCl₂ + 2 H₂O (or sodium bicarbonate, which decomposes to very reactive Na₂CO₃ above ≈ 140 °C). Removal depends on temperature, residence time, mixing and the stoichiometric ratio (often 1.5–3); the fabric filter cake adds further contact. No liquid effluent — the product is a dry powder; recirculation improves sorbent use.

video_tutorials.title: Dry Scrubber — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Dry Scrubber.
A dry scrubber removes acid gases by injecting fine dry sorbent — hydrated lime or sodium bicarbonate — into the flue gas.
The sorbent reacts with SO₂ and HCl in a reaction chamber; the dry product and unreacted sorbent are captured in a fabric filter, partly recirculated, and disposed of as powder with no wastewater.
Typical applications include waste incinerators, biomass and small coal boilers; glass, cement and metal furnaces.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Dry Scrubber works.
Sorbent is fed from the silo.
It is blown into the duct through lances.
Acid gases react in the chamber.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Dry Scrubber.
Check sorbent feed rate and stack emissions.
Clear lances; inspect silo vent.
Inspect reactor / ducts for deposits.
Watch for poor removal: emission high. Common cause: low feed, bad mixing, wrong temperature.
Watch for feeder bridging: no sorbent. Common cause: moisture.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
